what:
Native-module ABI strategy reference (research 2026-04-27, supports memories #348/#349): the bug class behind #348 is GENERIC to any V8-coupled native module in Node — not specific to better-sqlite3 or SQLite. Same failure shape would occur with bcrypt v4, canvas, sharp (older), node-pty, any module using NAN or direct V8 bindings. Standard ecosystem fixes, ranked by typicality for our shape (npm-distributed CLI/MCP server):

1. **N-API (Node-API) bindings** — single binary works across Node versions ≥ minimum N-API version. ABI guaranteed stable by Node itself. Examples: sqlite3 v5+, bcrypt v5+, libsql, sse4_crc32 (post-N-API migration). For SQLite specifically, **libsql (Turso) advertises drop-in better-sqlite3-compatible API + N-API**; sqlite3 v5+ also N-API but async-only.

2. **prebuildify + node-gyp-build** — ships ALL platform-specific prebuilts inside the npm package; no postinstall network call. Replaces the older prebuild-install (now unmaintained per its own README).

3. **Single Executable Applications (SEA)** — bundle Node runtime with script into one binary. Node 19+, maturing in 2026. Future option for aide-memory if we want zero-Node-dep distribution; not for 0.5.0.

4. **Electron-style runtime bundling** — desktop apps (Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code, Slack) bundle their own Node + use electron-rebuild. Doesn't apply to us (we're a CLI/MCP server, not a desktop app).

5. **Auto-rebuild on detected mismatch** — what I originally proposed. Novel, no clear prior art. Becomes a fallback only.

Pure-JS / WASM (sql.js) is positioned as the BROWSER/edge solution, not the CLI solution — explicitly recommended only "for browser-side SQLite" by 2026 surveys.

**Implication for aide-memory packaging decisions:** the modern ecosystem-standard answer to "how do we make a native-dep CLI work across user Node versions" is "use N-API bindings + ship prebuilts via prebuildify-style packaging." Switching from better-sqlite3 to libsql is not a lib-swap-and-pray — it's adopting the standard ABI-stability mechanism. Future native-dep choices (if we ever add another native module) should default to N-API bindings.
why: User pushed back ("is this really a lib issue?") and forced research into how production apps actually handle this class of bug. Findings are durable architectural knowledge: the bug class is Node-native-modules-generic, the ecosystem-standard answer is N-API, and the bucket of pseudo-solutions (auto-rebuild novelty, sql.js wrong-tool, SEA-future) are all ranked. Storing scoped to store.ts so future packaging/binding decisions can recall the framework without re-doing the research.
